chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Quran is a covenant of God to His creatures; thus it is befitting for the Muslim person that he looks into his covenant, and that he recites from it fifty verses every day.

key_terms.عَهْد: Covenant/pledge — a binding agreement; here it denotes the Quran as God's formal compact with humanity
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: It befits/is proper — an expression of strong recommendation, close to obligation
key_terms.يَنْظُر: To look into/contemplate — implies not just reading but reflecting upon

ai.seo_question: How many verses of the Quran should a Muslim recite each day according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the Quran as a divine covenant (ahd) — a binding contract between God and humanity — and on this basis instructs that every Muslim should engage with it daily, specifically reciting at least fifty verses. This framing of the Quran as a covenant would have resonated deeply with the early Muslim audience, who understood covenants as solemn obligations requiring regular renewal and attention. The number fifty ayat is a recommended minimum, understood in Shia tradition as a practical guideline for maintaining a living connection with the Quran.
